claims.statement: Both infliximab and cyclosporine are effective rescue therapies with similar outcomes; choice depends on provider experience and patient-specific factors
claims.evidence_excerpt: The CYSIF trial (Laharie 2012, n=115): treatment failure at day 98 was 60% (cyclosporine) vs 54% (infliximab), non-significant difference. claims.statement: Colectomy should be offered early for refractory disease; restorative proctocolectomy with IPAA is standard; staged procedures reduce complications

claims.statement: Methotrexate parenterally is effective for maintenance; biologics should be continued to maintain their induced remissions (R2.4-R2.7)
claims.evidence_excerpt: **MTX maintenance:** One RCT (Feagan 2000): after 16-24 weeks of 25 mg/week IM induction, patients randomized to 15 mg/week IM MTX vs. placebo for 40 weeks. Remission maintained: 65% vs. 39% (RR 1.67; 95% CI 1.05-2.67). Nausea/vomiting more common with MTX (40% vs. 25%); no severe leukopenia.

claims.statement: Vedolizumab and natalizumab are effective; natalizumab is restricted by PML risk (R27-R29)
claims.evidence_excerpt: Vedolizumab (gut-selective α4β7 integrin inhibitor): No cases of PML reported. May have slower onset than anti-TNF agents, particularly in anti-TNF-experienced patients.
